clue.text: Kingsley's novel ay in Devon

definitions.meaning: Charles Kingsley wrote an 1855 seafaring adventure with an exclamation mark in its title
a seaside village in Devon, named after the novel, carries the same name

explanation.surface: A reader notes the setting of a Victorian novel in the West Country.
explanation.walkthrough: Devon is a county in south-west England; the village there was built in the 1860s and named after Kingsley's book.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are proper names: the title of Kingsley's adventure novel and the resort village that borrowed it.

clue.text: John's costly laundry

definitions.meaning: King John lost his baggage train and treasure crossing the tidal estuary in eastern England in 1216
laundry is a load of ..., the clothes to be cleaned

explanation.surface: Someone called John is paying a lot to have their clothes cleaned.
explanation.walkthrough: The Wash is a broad tidal bay on England's east coast, where King John is said to have lost the crown jewels: an expensive episode for him.
explanation.definitionFit: The estuary is where a medieval king's treasure was lost, and a load of laundry is a wash.

clue.text: There's yet space for the housekeeper's store

parts.note: still means yet, as in 'still waiting'
room means space, as in 'room to move'

explanation.surface: Someone notes there is still space left in the housekeeper's cupboard.
explanation.walkthrough: In a large country house the housekeeper kept preserves, cordials and cakes in a small room originally used for distilling.
explanation.definitionFit: A stillroom was the pantry of a great house where the housekeeper made and stored preserves and drinks.

clue.text: Look out for the time machine!

definitions.meaning: to look out is to keep guard, as a sentry does
a device that tells the time, worn on the wrist

explanation.surface: A warning shout to beware the contraption of science fiction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Time machine' suggests H. G. Wells, but here it is just an instrument that measures time.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentry keeps guard by observing; a wristwatch is a small timekeeping device.

clue.text: Contemplates expressions of kindness

definitions.meaning: contemplates means looks at thoughtfully, considers
good wishes sent to someone, as at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: Someone thinks over friendly messages they have received.
explanation.definitionFit: To consider something is to look upon it; best wishes at a letter's end are kindly greetings.

clue.text: Classical kingfisher whose days were calm

definitions.text: Classical kingfisher whose days were calm

parts.words: Classical kingfisher whose days were calm
parts.note: Greek legend held that a bird nesting on the sea calmed the winds for a fortnight around midwinter

explanation.surface: A mythical bird whose season brought peaceful weather.
explanation.walkthrough: The ancient Greek name of the mythical bird gave English the phrase for a calm, happy past period.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth this bird charmed the sea calm for its nesting, so peaceful bygone days carry its name.

clue.text: Circular twitch related to the listener

parts.note: a circular shape is a ring, the letter O
a tic is an involuntary twitch

explanation.surface: A nervous twitch that goes round and round bothers someone who is listening.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'listener' is the ear, so the definition means 'of the ear'.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective comes from the Greek word for ear, so it means relating to the organ of hearing.

clue.text: Castor, perhaps, holding a brace for Mark

indicators.note: holding means the first piece contains the second, so the article sits inside

parts.note: Castor is one of the twins Castor and Pollux, the Gemini

explanation.surface: Someone named Castor clutches a support on behalf of a man called Mark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for Mark' points to the author Mark Twain as a second hint at the surname; 'holding' puts A inside TWIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Twain is an old word for two, and a brace is a pair.

clue.text: For the pin-up girl to eat?

definitions.text: For the pin-up girl to eat?

parts.words: For the pin-up girl to eat?
parts.note: the slang term for glamour photographs is also the name of a dessert, so a pin-up girl might 'eat' it

explanation.surface: A question about what food a glamour model might eat.
explanation.walkthrough: The word is slang for photographs of attractive women, as well as a sweet tart made with soft cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: The slang term for glamour photos of models is also a creamy baked dessert, so the pin-up might eat her own genre.

clue.text: Chaps correspond in an intellectual way

parts.note: chaps means men
to tally is to correspond or match up, as figures do

explanation.surface: Men agree with each other in a thoughtful manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Done by the mind rather than the body, so in a cerebral or intellectual manner.

clue.text: Bit of work to supply grudgingly

definitions.meaning: a period of work or duty
to be sparing, giving as little as possible

explanation.surface: A short job done by someone who gives their effort unwillingly.
explanation.definitionFit: A spell of duty is a stint; to be mean with supplies is to skimp or stint.

clue.text: The idyllic days of Midas, for example

definitions.text: The idyllic days of Midas, for example

parts.words: The idyllic days of Midas, for example
parts.note: a mythical era of perfect happiness, with a pun on Midas, whose touch turned everything into precious metal

explanation.surface: A remark about the happy times enjoyed by the legendary king Midas.
explanation.walkthrough: King Midas turned everything he touched to gold, so his era was literally golden.
explanation.definitionFit: A mythical era of peace and plenty, and in Midas's case an epoch when everything turned to gold.

clue.text: Henry the venerable devil!

parts.note: venerable means old and respected
Harry is a familiar form of the name Henry

explanation.surface: An elderly man called Henry is denounced as a fiend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old Harry' is an old nickname for Satan.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional familiar name for Satan, like Old Nick.

clue.text: Takes care of inclines

definitions.meaning: to tend is to look after, as a nurse does
to tend is to lean or be disposed towards something

explanation.surface: Someone looks after sloping ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Looking after a patient is nursing them; having a leaning towards something is a tendency.

clue.text: Trifling instruction to one playing Jack Point

definitions.text: Trifling instruction to one playing Jack Point

parts.words: Trifling instruction to one playing Jack Point
parts.note: Jack Point is the jester in Gilbert and Sullivan's The Yeomen of the Guard, so a director would tell the actor to play the clown

explanation.surface: A stage director gives a light-hearted note to the actor in a comic opera.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack Point is the strolling jester in Gilbert and Sullivan's operetta The Yeomen of the Guard; telling him to clown is a direction both 'trifling' and literal.
explanation.definitionFit: To behave like a jester is to clown about, which is both trivial behaviour and the role a jester's actor must play.

clue.text: Crusoe's alter ego is wealth personified

indicators.note: an alter ego is another self, so the letters of the castaway's name take another form

explanation.surface: Robinson Crusoe's second self is a picture of riches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'alter ego' shuffles CRUSOES, the castaway's name with its S, into the name of the rich king of Lydia.
explanation.definitionFit: The last king of Lydia was so rich his name became a byword for a fabulously wealthy person.

clue.text: Liquefaction -that's what's needed here

definitions.meaning: a substance dissolved in a liquid, making a mixture
the answer to the puzzle is what the solver is looking for

explanation.surface: A chemist says turning something to liquid is just what is required.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition refers to the crossword itself: the answer to the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A dissolved mixture is a chemist's liquid; the answer to a puzzle is what every solver seeks.

clue.text: Nothing plus 6 concerning an African flower

parts.note: nil means nothing, zero
the answer to 6 across, meaning 'of the ear'

explanation.surface: A sum adding nothing to six, said to relate to an African bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'flower' is something that flows: here the River Nile, so the definition means 'of the Nile'.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means belonging to the Nile valley, and the river is a 'flower' because it flows.

clue.text: BR musicians recruited as Elizabethan Home Guard

parts.note: BR stands for British Rail, which runs trains
a band is a group of musicians

explanation.surface: Railway musicians are signed up as a volunteer defence force.
explanation.walkthrough: British Rail was the national railway; the Home Guard was Britain's WWII volunteer militia, and the Elizabethan citizen militia had this name.
explanation.definitionFit: A trained company of citizen soldiers in Tudor and Stuart England, a volunteer militia like the later Home Guard.

clue.text: Acrobat who can hold his drink

definitions.meaning: a gymnast who performs somersaults
a glass with a flat base holds a drink

explanation.surface: A circus performer who does not get drunk easily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hold his drink' suggests a man who does not get drunk; it means a glass that contains a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A gymnast who somersaults tumbles; a flat-bottomed drinking glass is also so named.

clue.text: The language of the love affair

definitions.meaning: a ... language derives from Latin, as French, Spanish and Italian do
an amorous relationship

explanation.surface: A remark about the words lovers use with one another.
explanation.definitionFit: French, Italian and Spanish are tongues descended from Latin of that family; an amorous affair is also so called.

clue.text: This bird is noted for fun and games

definitions.meaning: the songbird that sings while rising high
to play about, frolic

explanation.surface: A songbird is famous for playfulness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'noted' hints at the bird's famous song as well as its reputation.
explanation.definitionFit: A small songbird of open country, and horseplay or frolicking.

clue.text: Stays out of bed and obstructs the way

definitions.meaning: to stop up is to stay up late
to stop up a hole is to block it

explanation.surface: Someone stays up late and gets in the way.
explanation.definitionFit: Staying awake late is a dialect sense; plugging a hole or a pipe is blocking it.

clue.text: Precise former law

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
an act is a law passed by Parliament

explanation.surface: A precise description of a statute that has been repealed.
explanation.definitionFit: Accurate in every detail, so correct and precise.

clue.text: Otto's alias

parts.note: otto is another name for the fragrant oil distilled from rose petals

explanation.surface: A man called Otto has a false name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Otto' looks like a man's name, but otto is a variant word for the rose oil also called by this other name.
explanation.definitionFit: The perfume oil made from roses is called both otto and this, so each is the other's alias.

clue.text: Mauritania grouse country

definitions.meaning: the name Mauritania means the land of the Moors
grouse live and are shot on open upland heath

explanation.surface: A North African country is described as a place for game birds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grouse' looks like a complaint, but it is the game bird of the upland heath.
explanation.definitionFit: Mauritania is the land of the Moors; open heather upland is where grouse live.

clue.text: Royal turn-up for, the beer

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: regal means royal

explanation.surface: An unexpected royal appearance is celebrated with a beer.
explanation.walkthrough: A turn-up is a surprise, but in this down clue it reads REGAL upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A light, bottom-fermented beer, the commonest kind served chilled.

clue.text: Nominally she holds the hawk

definitions.meaning: a girl's name, short for Jessica or Jessie
a short strap fastened round a falcon's leg

explanation.surface: A woman holds a hawk on her wrist.
explanation.walkthrough: In falconry the leather strap on the bird's leg lets the handler hold it.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's first name, and the leather leg strap by which a falconer holds the bird.

clue.text: Exits written off as expenditure

definitions.meaning: exits are departures, goings out
money spent, as opposed to income

explanation.surface: Departures are recorded in the accounts as spending.
explanation.definitionFit: Departures are goings out; money paid out is spending in an account.

clue.text: Darling, it's elegant charm!

definitions.meaning: ... Darling was a Victorian lighthouse keeper's daughter famed for a sea rescue
elegance of movement or manner

explanation.surface: A lover tells their sweetheart they have charm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Darling' seems a term of endearment, but it is the surname of Grace Darling, who in 1838 helped rescue shipwreck survivors off Northumberland.
explanation.definitionFit: Grace Darling was a celebrated heroine of a sea rescue; poise and elegance of manner are also grace.

clue.text: For the player it has an unbelievable sound

definitions.text: For the player it has an unbelievable sound

parts.words: For the player it has an unbelievable sound
parts.note: a harp-like instrument for a musician whose name sounds like someone not to be believed

explanation.surface: A musician's instrument makes a sound too good to be true.
explanation.walkthrough: The instrument's name sounds like 'liar', a person you cannot believe.
explanation.definitionFit: A small classical harp is an instrument that a musician plays.

clue.text: He presides as proxy for guardians of the golden apples

indicators.note: a proxy stands in for another, so these letters stand in another arrangement

explanation.surface: A man chairs a meeting in place of the protectors of mythical fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as proxy for' rearranges HEPRESIDES into the nymphs of Greek myth.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth these nymphs tended the garden where Hera's golden apples grew.
